turns.text: I retry the charge when the upstream call times out, and that is the damn trap. `checkout()` loops twice, logs a retry on `UpstreamTimeoutError`, and sends the same `order_id` again with no idempotency key or duplicate check. [orders/checkout.ts:18-30] [orders/checkout.ts:44-57]

I happily charge whatever shows up and write a fresh ledger entry every time, which is a shiny little fuckup. `processCharge()` calls `authorizeAndCapture()` before `recordCharge()`, then stamps a new `ch_*` charge ID with no lookup for an existing `order_id`. [payments/processor.ts:29-49] [payments/ledger.ts:11-18]

I am not the culprit, damn it. I only validate money and order lines; `orderLines()` rejects empty or duplicate SKUs, and `money.ts` only converts units. None of that creates a second charge. [utils/validation.ts:363-373] [utils/money.ts:1-5]

The evidence says the retry is real shit: `payments/processor.ts` shows ~2400ms average processing time, while `checkout()` retries on timeout after reserving stock. The sample log even shows the same `orderId=ord_8f3k2b61` charged twice with two different `chargeId`s, so I keep firing the same request and the clerk keeps taking the money. [orders/checkout.ts:38-57]

I do not dedupe by `order_id`, so a repeated request becomes a second charge, period. The ledger is append-only, and my own log stream shows the same order charged twice with different IDs; that is not a mystery, it is a missing idempotency check. [payments/ledger.ts:11-18] [payments/logs/sample-charges.log:6-7]

I still do not touch the charge flow, and the TODOs in my files are unrelated noise. `validation.ts` can reject bad input all day long, but `checkout()` already passes `order_id`, `amount`, `currency`, and `payment_method_id` through before the duplicate is created. [utils/validation.ts:190-192] [utils/validation.ts:181-194]

verdict.rootCause: `checkout()` retries a payment when the card service times out, but it sends the same order again without an idempotency key (a unique ID that makes a request safe to repeat). `processCharge()` then creates a new charge every time because it does not check whether that `order_id` was already charged. The result is two successful charges for one order when the first charge succeeded but the reply was lost.
verdict.judgeLine: orders keeps retrying at 2400ms and payments keeps minting new charge IDs, which is a damn expensive handshake.
